name: Hamititan
sum: Hamititan is a titanosaur from the Early Cretaceous Shengjinkou Formation of Xinjiang, China, found in a lake deposit with exceptional preservation.
wsnote: No body-size figure was read in the sources consulted.
holotype: HM V22; four sacral elements (IVPP V27875) were not referred.
material: Known from the holotype; a theropod tooth lay near the sixth caudal vertebra.
exceptional: Preserved in a Konservat-Lagerstatte lake deposit.
biology: A theropod probably fed on the carcass shortly after death, judging by the tooth found beside the holotype.
author: Wang et al. 2021

images.caption: Skeletal reconstruction of Hamititan xinjiangensis showing the preserved bones.

sources.text: Wang X, Bandeira KL, Qiu R, Jiang S, Cheng X, Ma Y, Kellner AW 2021. The first dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous Hami Pterosaur Fauna, China. Scientific Reports 11(1). doi:10.1038/s41598-021-94273-7
